reasons: Lake record is verified and identifies the case as Muehler v. Mena, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2005-03-22.
Lake citations list official cite 544 U.S. 93, parallel cites 125 S. Ct. 1465 and 161 L. Ed. 2d 299, and vendor-neutral cite 2005 U.S. LEXIS 2755.
The opinion states that a SWAT team was used to secure the residence and grounds before the search.
The opinion discusses officer command of the situation, guarding detainees, and handcuffing during warrant execution, supporting a related scene-securing classification.
residual_risks: The body's Appears on section says Securing the Scene — Key — Progeny / Refinement, which conflicts with the front-matter/inventory role of Related; no separate inventory row was supplied for that rendered assertion.

defect.evidence_quote: However, the 2- to 3-hour detention in handcuffs in this case does not outweigh the government's continuing safety interests.
defect.problem: The holding is broadly phrased as if a weapons/gang-house warrant categorically permits handcuffing occupants for the entire search. The opinion supports that result on the facts of this case, emphasizing the 2-to-3-hour duration, continuing safety interests, dangerous-weapons search, wanted gang member, and multiple detainees.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten to: Officers executing a warrant to search a gang house for weapons may, under Muehler's circumstances, detain occupants in handcuffs for the 2-to-3-hour duration of the search when continuing safety interests justify it.

reasons: The opinion says Mena's detention for the duration of the search was reasonable under Summers because a warrant existed and she was an occupant.
The opinion separately says the use of handcuffs was reasonable because this was no ordinary search: the warrant authorized a weapons search and a wanted gang member resided on the premises.
residual_risks: Duration remains fact-sensitive; the opinion says duration can affect the Graham balance and declined to address detention beyond completion of search tasks.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the case-specific limits: 2-to-3-hour search duration, ongoing safety interests, warrant for weapons, wanted gang member, and multiple detainees.

reasons: The opinion directly concerns detaining occupants during execution of a search warrant.
The opinion applies and refines Summers by addressing handcuffs as reasonable force and questioning during an already lawful detention.
residual_risks: The case is primarily about detention/seizure at the scene, not a search of Mena's person; the home title includes detention, so the role remains supported.
